advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Limit write_release_alerts to in-scope tickets (or skip it) when ctx.filter_local_ids / ctx.selection_ids is set
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:151: if release_withheld_sink and ctx.persist:

src/rebar/reconciler/apply_phase.py:63-66: 'when filter_local_ids is set, discard mutations that target tickets outside the filter scope. All three differs ran on their full, unfiltered inputs ... only the dispatch set is narrowed.'

src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:65-68: 'Scoped and no-write passes skip recovery: it can finalize bindings and issue remote label/property writes outside their permitted boundary.' / if not scoped_ids and ctx.persist:
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:48: scoped_ids = ctx.filter_local_ids or ctx.selection_ids
advisory.finding: Release BRIDGE_ALERT events are written for every ticket in release_withheld_sink, gated only on ctx.persist. Scoped passes (filter_local_ids / selection_ids) run the differs over all local tickets and narrow only the dispatch set, so a filtered pass writes alert events to tickets outside its scope.
scenarios: An operator runs a `--filter-local-ids X` pass and BRIDGE_ALERT open/resolve events are written to unrelated tickets Y and Z whose releases are withheld.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute `scoped_ids` as already done at line 48 and either skip alert writes when scoped, or filter `release_withheld_sink` to `local_id in scoped_ids` before calling write_release_alerts.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude withheld-only updates from the RECON outbound_differ totals and the outbound_update log line (count only dispatchable updates)
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py:311-318: if ( fields or comment_mutations or label_mutations or link_mutations or release_mutations or withheld ):
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py:319-320: '# Log changed field names ... to expose non-converging updates'
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:163: _ob_updates = sum(1 for m in outbound_raw if m.action == "update")
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:166: f"RECON: outbound_differ total={len(outbound_raw)} "
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:188-189: if not _has_dispatchable_update(om): continue
tests/external/live_jira_dc/_bridge_output.py:86-90: if any(outbound) or any(inbound): return (... '— a converged repeat pass must compute nothing')
advisory.finding: A bound update that only withholds releases is still added to outbound_raw and counted in the `RECON: outbound_differ total=/update=` telemetry, and it prints a `RECON: outbound_update` line every pass. It is only dropped at typed-mutation construction. A ticket whose version stays missing therefore reports a non-zero outbound total on every steady-state pass, and the live harness no-op check treats that as computed work.
scenarios: A release names a version that does not exist yet; every later pass prints `outbound_differ total=1 update=1` and an outbound_update line even though nothing is dispatched, so the live wrote_nothing_problem check fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute the RECON counts with `_has_dispatchable_update` (e.g. `_ob_updates = sum(1 for m in outbound_raw if m.action == 'update' and _has_dispatchable_update(m))`, and the total likewise). In the builder, print the outbound_update line only when something besides `withheld` is non-empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the BRIDGE_ALERT row in docs/event-schema.md to list `rebar.reconciler.release_alerts.write_release_alerts` as a producer and describe the release-version-missing and release-version-archived alerts it opens and resolves (ADR 0124 decisions 8 and 9).
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/release_alerts.py:131: `_write_event_file(tracker_dir, local_id, "BRIDGE_ALERT", record)` writes a BRIDGE_ALERT event for each planned record. The records come from plan_release_alerts (release_alerts.py:100-110): `{"reason": ..., "tag": ...}` to open an alert and `{"resolved": True, "resolves_uuid": ..., "reason": ...}` to resolve one.
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:150-156 calls release_alerts.write_release_alerts on every persisted pass that has withheld-release records.
docs/event-schema.md:39 says 'The producer column identifies maintained Python seams that own event construction.'

docs/event-schema.md:59: '| `BRIDGE_ALERT` | `rebar.reconciler.dispatch_one.create_one` | Adds or resolves a Jira bridge alert in `state.bridge_alerts`. The producer records a retained Jira issue whose post-create identity write failed. |'
Searching src/rebar for BRIDGE_ALERT finds only two reconciler write sites: dispatch_one.py:248 and the new release_alerts.py:131. The row was complete before this change and is incomplete after it.
advisory.finding: The change adds `rebar.reconciler.release_alerts.write_release_alerts` as a new producer of BRIDGE_ALERT ticket events. These events carry `release-version-missing:<name>`, `release-version-archived:<name>`, or resolution records with `resolves_uuid`. The BRIDGE_ALERT row in docs/event-schema.md still names only `rebar.reconciler.dispatch_one.create_one` as its producer. It also describes the event only as recording a retained Jira issue whose post-create identity write failed.
scenarios: A contributor or operator who checks the event-schema inventory to see what writes BRIDGE_ALERT events, or what a `release-version-*` alert means, finds only the identity-write-failure producer.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/event-schema.md:59, add `rebar.reconciler.release_alerts.write_release_alerts` to the Produced by column. Extend the effect text to say that the release-sync producer opens one alert per withheld release, with reason `release-version-missing:<name>` or `release-version-archived:<name>`, and resolves it with a `resolves_uuid` record once the release is no longer withheld, citing ADR 0124.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the failed-read integration test discriminating: assert the add is attempted under unknown availability, and set up a state where a known read would resolve or raise an alert, then assert it does not.
evidence: tests/integration/reconciler/test_reconcile_releases_roundtrip.py:282: del state.project_versions["REB"]  # the fake now raises: availability unknown
tests/integration/reconciler/test_reconcile_releases_roundtrip.py:285-286: assert _alert_events(git_repo) == events / assert _open_release_alerts(git_repo) == ["release-version-missing:2.4"]

The same two post-conditions hold in test_missing_version_is_withheld_alerted_and_written_once_it_exists pass 2, where availability is KNOWN (versions=()), so neither assertion separates the two worlds.

release_alerts.py docstring: 'A project whose read fails is left out (unknown): the diff then behaves as before this rule' — under unknown, outbound_releases._split_releases emits {"action": "add"}, but the test does not assert _fix_version_writes(state).
advisory.finding: test_failed_version_read_writes_and_resolves_no_alert cannot tell 'availability unknown' apart from 'availability known, version still missing'. Its post-conditions (alert-event count unchanged, the missing:2.4 alert still open) are exactly the steady state that a successful read with an empty version list also produces (pass 2 of the lifecycle test shows this). So the test stays green if the read failure is cached, ignored, or treated as an empty list. It also never asserts the documented unknown-path behaviour 'nothing is withheld' (the add is attempted).
scenarios: A regression that maps a failed read to {} (known, empty) still shows the alert open with no new events, so the test passes.
A regression that skips the version read entirely while keeping last pass's withheld result also passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the del, assert `_fix_version_writes(state) == ["add_fix_version(REB-1,2.4)"]` (unknown availability means nothing is withheld). Alternatively, remove 2.4 locally before the failed-read pass, so a known read would plan a resolution, then assert the alert stays open.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a liveness anchor to the preview-pass test (e.g. a following persist pass that writes the alert, or an assertion on the dry-run result) before trusting the absence assertions.
evidence: tests/integration/reconciler/test_reconcile_releases_roundtrip.py:298-300: run_pass(state, target_mode=Mode.DRY_RUN) / assert _alert_events(git_repo) == events / assert _open_release_alerts(git_repo) == []
The return value of reconcile_once (returned by run_pass) is discarded; no presence assertion comes from the same pass.
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:151: if release_withheld_sink and ctx.persist: — the gate under test only matters if the sink was filled, which the test never confirms.
advisory.finding: test_preview_pass_writes_no_alert is absence-only: the event count is unchanged and no release alert is open. Nothing in it shows the DRY_RUN pass actually reached the outbound release diff and withheld 2.4. If a preview pass stopped before the version read or the outbound differ, or failed quietly, the test would still pass, so it cannot show that the ctx.persist gate is what stops the write.
scenarios: If the preview pass raised internally or never diffed the ticket, both absences hold trivially.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the DRY_RUN assertions, run a normal `run_pass(state)` and assert `_open_release_alerts(git_repo) == ["release-version-missing:2.4"]`. This proves the same setup does produce an alert when persisting, so the preview absence is meaningful.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the static scan covered real files (root.is_dir() and a non-empty file list including outbound_releases.py) before asserting no hits.
evidence: tests/unit/reconciler/test_release_alerts.py:140: root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "src" / "rebar" / "reconciler"
tests/unit/reconciler/test_release_alerts.py:144: for p in sorted(root.rglob("*.py"))
tests/unit/reconciler/test_release_alerts.py:148: assert hits == []
No assertion that root exists or that the scanned file list is non-empty.
advisory.finding: test_no_reconciler_code_creates_a_jira_version is an absence check (`hits == []`) over a file walk with no check that any file was scanned. If the `parents[3]` root resolves wrongly (test moved, src layout changed) or rglob matches nothing, the scan is empty and the test passes. The regex also misses version-create call shapes other than the literal `create_version` or a `/rest/api/N/version` string.
scenarios: The test file is relocated one directory deeper: root points at a nonexistent path, rglob yields nothing, and the test passes regardless of reconciler contents.
advisory.suggested_fix: Collect `files = sorted(root.rglob("*.py"))`, then `assert root.is_dir() and any(p.name == "outbound_releases.py" for p in files)` before computing hits.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Run check_store_compat before writing release alerts, or move the alert writes into/after the apply phase
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/apply_phase.py:52-60: 'fail CLOSED on a store this rebar cannot interpret BEFORE any mutation' / if persist: ... check_store_compat(tracker_dir(repo_root))
src/rebar/reconciler/release_alerts.py:131: _write_event_file(tracker_dir, local_id, "BRIDGE_ALERT", record)
search `_write_event_file(` in src/rebar/reconciler: all other callers are in apply_inbound_events.py (lines 109, 142, 164, 243, 289, 313, 400, 460)
dropped.finding: write_release_alerts writes ticket events (via _write_event_file) during the outbound differ phase. That is before the apply phase's fail-closed check_store_compat gate, which is meant to run before any mutation, and every other _write_event_file caller is in the apply phase.
scenarios: The tracker store was written by a newer, incompatible rebar; the pass appends BRIDGE_ALERT events to it in the differ phase before apply_mutations raises on the compat check.
dropped.suggested_fix: Defer write_release_alerts until after check_store_compat succeeds (e.g. stash the sink on ctx and write it in the apply/persist phase), or call check_store_compat(tracker_dir) inside the `ctx.persist` branch before writing.
